chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Jibraeel (peace be upon him) said: 'We do not enter a house in which there is a picture, nor a dog, meaning the picture of a human, nor a house in which there are statues.'
ai.seo_question: What types of images and animals prevent angels from entering a house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle that the presence of images (surah) and dogs impedes the entry of angels, a ruling derived from Jibraeel’s (AS) report. Shia scholars, including Al-Hilli and Al-Majlisi, interpret 'surah' broadly to include two-dimensional depictions of animate beings, while 'tamathil' specifically denotes three-dimensional statues, linking this physical state of the home to spiritual receptivity. The prohibition underscores the concept of 'ghurrah' (divine honor) being withdrawn from a household due to idolatrous associations or distraction from worship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said: ‘We (the Angels) neither enter a house in which there is a picture, nor a dog, meaning pictures of the humans, nor a house wherein are statues’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ‘Uthman from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Jibril has said, ‘We do not enter a house in which there are pictures, or a dog, that is, pictures of human beings or a house in which statues exist.’”
